items.title: Complete retarded point fields: unique retarded root, the delta substitution with denominator $1-n\cdot\beta$, Liénard-Wiechert potentials and fields, and a uniform far-zone remainder
items.design_state: complete-exact-declared-branch-conditional-research-argument; direct dependency list reconciled with the actual proof uses and the root clause stated in event form (batch-22 notes)
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), used through the change-of-variables corollaries inside the proof of the retarded-convolution identity cited in clause (b) ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $c>0$, let $v_*<c$, let $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^3$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$, put $\mu_0:=(c^2\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$ and $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$, and write $\Omega:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and $\Gamma:=\{(z(s),s):s\in\mathbb R\}$.

(a) [Root and emission-time Jacobian] For every $(x,t)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ (equivalently $x\ne z(t)$) there is exactly one $s=s(x,t)<t$ with $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$. The map $s:\Omega\setminus\Gamma\to\mathbb R$ is of class $C^3$, and with $R:=x-z(s)$, $r:=|R|$, $n:=R/r$, $\beta:=z'(s)/c$ and $\kappa:=1-n\cdot\beta$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) one has $$\partial_ts(x,t)=\kappa^{-1},\qquad \nabla_xs(x,t)=-\frac{n}{c\,\kappa},\qquad \kappa\in[1-v_*/c,\,1+v_*/c],$$ so $\kappa\ge 1-v_*/c>0$ uniformly on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$. Moreover, for the fixed $x$ and near the root, the function $s'\mapsto s'+|x-z(s')|/c$ is differentiable at $s'=s$ with derivative $\kappa(x,t)$: this emission-time Jacobian $1-n\cdot\beta$ is the denominator produced by the delta substitution of clause (b).

(b) [Delta substitution and Liénard-Wiechert potentials] Let $\rho,J\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ be the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] attached to $q$ and the worldline $z$, let $K$ be the retarded wave kernel of [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]], and for $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ put $(K\circledast\psi)(y,\tau):=\langle K,\psi(y+\cdot,\tau+\cdot)\rangle$ and define the retarded-history pairings by the explicit integrals $\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle:=(q/\varepsilon_0)\int_{\mathbb R}(K\circledast\psi)(z(s),s)\,ds$, $\langle\Upsilon,\psi\rangle:=\mu_0q\int_{\mathbb R}z'(s)(K\circledast\psi)(z(s),s)\,ds$, componentwise in the second case. These are the history-integral interpretation supplied by clause(b) of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]], not ordinary distribution action on a noncompact test. Then these pairings are finite for every $\psi$ and their exact retarded-convolution values are $$\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}\frac{C\,\psi}{\kappa\,r}\,dx\,dt,\qquad \langle\Upsilon,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}\frac{\beta}{c}\,\frac{C\,\psi}{\kappa\,r}\,dx\,dt$$ (the second identity componentwise); equivalently, $\Phi$ and $\Upsilon$ are the regular distributions of the locally integrable zero extensions to $\Gamma$ of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi:=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A:=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$. The weight $(\kappa r)^{-1}$ with $\kappa=1-n\cdot\beta$ is the exact form of the substitution with denominator $1-n\cdot\beta$ (the rigorous statement is the displayed pairing identity; composition of $\delta$ with a function is not part of the distribution calculus used here).

(c) [Fields and the velocity/acceleration split] With $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), and writing $\dot\beta:=z''(s)/c$ at the root, $$E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{vel}}=\frac{C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)}{\kappa^3r^2},\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta\bigr)}{c\,\kappa^3r},\qquad B=\frac{n\times E}{c}$$ at every event of $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Both $E$ and $B$ are $C^1$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, and the velocity field obeys the bound $$|E_{\mathrm{vel}}(x,t)|\le |C|\,\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}\,r(x,t)^{-2}$$ at every event.

(d) [Uniform far-zone remainder] For every $s_0\in\mathbb R$ and every $n\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|n|=1$, put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$ and $t_r:=s_0+r/c$ for $r>0$, and set $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\dot\beta_0:=z''(s_0)/c$, $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Then $(x_r,t_r)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ and $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$ for every $r>0$, and $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0\bigr)}{c\,\kappa_0^3\,r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c},$$ where the remainder is bounded uniformly in the direction, $$|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le |C|\,\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}\,r^{-2}\qquad\text{for every }n\in S^2\text{ and every }r>0.$$ Equivalently, $rE(x_r,t_r)\to C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\,\kappa_0^3)$ as $r\to\infty$, uniformly over $n\in S^2$ at the explicit rate $O(r^{-1})$ given by the same bound multiplied by $r$. The uniformity is in the direction $n$ at a fixed emission event $s_0$; no uniformity in $s_0$ is asserted ($z''$ is not assumed bounded), and no finite-energy, decay or radiation-flux conclusion is drawn.

This is a mathematical model computation for the stipulated $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline and the retarded choice; no self-force law, no radiation-reaction postulate and no physical Maxwell coupling is asserted or proved, and the uniform speed bound and the exclusion of $\Gamma$ are essential hypotheses (see the companion example page).

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix $c>0$, $v_*<c$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $\varepsilon_0>0$, $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ and a $C^3$ worldline $z$ with $|z'|\le v_*$ everywhere. (a) Fix $(x,t)$ with $x
e z(t)$ and put $f(s):=t-s-|x-z(s)|/c$. Then $f$ is continuous, $f(t)=-|x-z(t)|/c<0$, and for $s_2>s_1$ the integral representation of $z(s_2)-z(s_1)$ with the integral triangle inequality ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]]) gives $|z(s_2)-z(s_1)|\le v_*(s_2-s_1)$, hence $f(s_2)-f(s_1)\le-(1-v_*/c)(s_2-s_1)<0$: $f$ is strictly decreasing. Since $|z(s)|\le|z(0)|+v_*|s|$ makes $f(s)	o+\infty$ as $s	o-\infty$, the intermediate value theorem ([[thm-intermediate-value]]) on an interval $[s_1,t]$ with $f(s_1)>0$ produces a root $s<t$, and strict decrease makes it unique. This is the $C^3$ branch of [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] applied in its corrected event form, which clauses (b)-(d) need because the root must be available at every event of $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, including events whose spatial point $x$ lies on the worldline at another time. At the root $r=c(t-s)>0$, so $s'\mapsto|x-z(s')|$ is near $s$ a composition of the $C^3$ map $s'\mapsto x-z(s')$ with the smooth norm off the origin ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); therefore $F(x,t,s):=t-s-|x-z(s)|/c$ is $C^3$ near $(x,t,s)$ and $\partial_sF=-\kappa\le-(1-v_*/c)<0$ there. The parametrized implicit function theorem with $C^3$ regularity ([[thm-parametrized-implicit-function-theorem-with-higher-regularity]]) supplies a local $C^3$ root map with $Ds=-(\partial_sF)^{-1}D_{(x,t)}F$, and global uniqueness identifies the local maps, so $s$ is $C^3$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$. Differentiating $F=0$ gives $\partial_ts=\kappa^{-1}$ and $
abla_xs=-n/(c\kappa)$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). The emission-time derivative is the one-variable chain rule applied to $s'\mapsto s'+|x-z(s')|/c$: its derivative is $1-n(s')\cdot eta(s')$, which at $s'=s$ equals $\kappa$; and $|n\cdot eta|\le| eta|\le v_*/c<1$ gives $\kappa\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). (b) is exactly clause (b) of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]], which supplies the finiteness of the pairings, the pairing identities and the identification of $\Phi,\Upsilon$ as the regular distributions of the locally integrable zero extensions of the $C^2$ potentials $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A= eta\varphi/c$ (its proof bounds the explicit history integrals on a fixed-support observation cylinder, uses integrability of $1/|y|$ near zero, and applies the actual nonnegative-Borel and L1 $C^1$ change-of-variables suppliers; the exact consumed statement is the displayed pairing identity, since the library does not define $\delta\circ f$). (c) is clause (c) of the same item together with the elementary bounds: $|1-| eta|^2|\le1$, $|n- eta|\le1+v_*/c$ and $\kappa^3\ge(1-v_*/c)^3$ give $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le |C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$; the split and $B=n	imes E/c$ are read off that clause, and the cross-product identities used to recognise the acceleration numerator are in [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]. (d) For fixed $s_0$ and unit $n$, the same Lipschitz bound gives $|z(t_r)-z(s_0)|\le v_*(t_r-s_0)=v_*r/c<r=|x_r-z(s_0)|$, so $x_r
e z(t_r)$ and $(x_r,t_r)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$; since $t_r-s_0=r/c=|x_r-z(s_0)|/c$, the time $s_0$ is a root at that event, and uniqueness from (a) gives $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$. Evaluating (c) at that event with $ eta= eta_0$, $\dot eta=\dot eta_0$, $\kappa=\kappa_0$ and retarded distance $r$ gives the displayed expansion with remainder $E_{\mathrm{vel}}$, whose bound is that of (c); multiplying the field error by $r$ gives the equivalent uniform limit. No uniformity in $s_0$ is claimed because $z''$ is not assumed bounded, and no clause asserts a self-force, radiation reaction, finite energy or physical Maxwell coupling. For the all-time history the point-current proper-graph hypothesis is automatic: compact ambient support bounds its time projection. The signed constant C remains in every field formula; absolute-value estimates use |C|. The witness q=−4pi epsilon0,z=0 gives |E_vel|=r^−2 while a signed-C upper bound would be negative.

items.title: Explicit mathematical hypothesis/convention examples
items.statement:
For clause(i) assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Euclidean box-measure interface; the direct root counterexamples in(ii),(iii) are choice-free. (i) [Plane-wave solutions with infinite spatial $L^2$ norm] Let $c>0$ and $W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ as in [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. For every $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ the function $u:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $u(x,t):=f(x_1-ct)$, is of class $C^\infty$ and satisfies $Wu=0$ identically. If $f\ne0$, then for every $t$ the level set $\{x:u(x,t)\ne0\}=(ct+U)\times\mathbb R^2$, where $U:=\{s\in\mathbb R:f(s)\ne0\}$ is nonempty and open, is unbounded, and $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(x,t)|^2\,dx=+\infty$. Consequently the smooth-data existence and smoothness clause (a) of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] carries no global finite-energy or decay conclusion: compact support of the data is a genuine hypothesis of its clause (d), not a consequence of smoothness.

(ii) [Failure of root existence without the uniform speed bound] Let $c>0$, $a>0$ and $z(s):=(\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2},0,0)$. Then $z$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with $|z'(s)|=\dfrac{c^2|s|}{\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2}}<c$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$, while $\sup_{s\in\mathbb R}|z'(s)|=c$; so there is no $v_*<c$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for all $s$: the worldline is subluminal at every finite time but has no uniform subluminal bound. For the observation $(x,t)=(0,0)$ there is no root $s<t$ of $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$: the equation would read $-s=\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2}/c$ with $s<0$, and squaring gives $s^2=s^2+a^2/c^2$, i.e. $a=0$, a contradiction. Thus the existence clause of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] genuinely needs its hypothesis $|z'|\le v_*<c$; the substitution denominator degenerates along this curve in the same limit.

(iii) [The event must lie off the worldline] Let $z$ be of class $C^1$ with $|z'|\le v_*<c$, and let $x=z(t)$ for some $t\in\mathbb R$. Then $s=t$ solves $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$ trivially, and the strict decrease of $s\mapsto t-s-|x-z(s)|/c$ shows that no root $s<t$ exists; hence the exclusion of the worldline $\Gamma$ in clause (a) of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] is a genuine hypothesis.

These are explicit mathematical checks of hypotheses and conventions of the wave and retarded-root results; no measurement, physical field identification or empirical claim is made.

(ii) Set $g(s):=\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2}>0$, so $g^2=c^2s^2+a^2$ and differentiation gives $2gg'=2c^2s$, i.e. $g'=c^2s/g$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); hence $z$ is $C^\infty$ with $z'(s)=(c^2s/g(s),0,0)$ and $|z'(s)|=c^2|s|/g(s)$. Then $|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s$ because $c^2s^2<c^2s^2+a^2$, while $|z'(s)|=c\,c|s|/\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2}	o c$ as $s	o\pm\infty$; so no $v_*<c$ bounds $|z'|$ uniformly. At $(x,t)=(0,0)$ a root would satisfy $-s=\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2}/c$; the left side is positive only for $s<0$, and squaring gives $s^2=s^2+a^2/c^2$, i.e. $a=0$, so no root exists. This is the curve of the design's X8 counterexample, restated as a pure mathematical check; it also exhibits the collapse of the substitution denominator's uniform lower bound, since with $x=0$ one has $n(s)=-e_1$ and $ eta(s)	o-e_1$ as $s	o-\infty$, so $\kappa=1-n\cdot eta	o0$. (iii) For $x=z(t)$ the value $s=t$ solves the equation, and for $s<t$ the C^1 branch of [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]], or its strict-decrease proof for $s\mapsto t-s-|x-z(s)|/c$, gives $t-s-|x-z(s)|/c>0$, so there is no root below $t$; the domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ is therefore the correct one. No clause of (i)-(iii) invokes or contradicts the physical interpretation of the fields. In(i), the finite box volumes used in the lower bound are exactly [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] under the stated Countable Choice. In(ii), smoothness of the positive square root is [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]. The root counterexample and strict-decrease argument themselves require no measure assumption.
